_label: MODELED SIMULATION DATA. Built to be consistent with the case study's 250-room modeled hotel and decision trace D-0418 (231 of 250 rooms, Saturday breakfast). Not data from a real hotel.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Expected covers = occupied rooms x trailing 4-Saturday covers per occupied room.
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Case study gives 231 rooms and 420 covers but no forecasting method.
Case study uses confidence qualitatively only.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Low-confidence cutoff = 80%. Below it the system may only recommend.
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Case study: 'Low confidence -> Recommend only' with no number.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Service buffer 8% above expected consumption; 3% for chronic-overproduction groups; 12% for groups with repeated stockouts.
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Needed to size production; not in the case study.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Chronic overproduction = leftover above 20% in at least 3 of the last 4 same-day services.
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Waste Agent needs a detection rule.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Production-change risk: |change| <= 10% LOW (delegable range, case study p.7), <= 25% MEDIUM, > 25% HIGH. Banquet guarantee changes are always HIGH.
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Case study defines the 10% range and the tiers, not the MEDIUM/HIGH boundary.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Inventory feed is stale when older than 12 hours.
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Case study: 'Inventory feed stale -> Block execution' with no age limit.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Abnormal event demand = event covers changed by more than 25% versus guarantee.
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Case study: 'Abnormal event demand -> Human review' with no number.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Agents conflict when Demand points up (> +5%) and the production draft points down (< -5%), or the reverse. Resolved only if Waste Agent evidence explains it; otherwise escalate.
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Mirrors the case study's pastry conflict example (p.4).

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Guest F&B score for the day = recent baseline minus 0.05 for each item group that stocks out.
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Links availability to the guest guardrail; not in the case study.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Policy: no item group may be planned below 100% of expected consumption (no planned stockouts).
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Hard constraint protecting the guest-experience floor.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Policy: carry-over stock is usable only inside its shelf life.
Authority levels: gate PASS -> DELEGATED (low-risk reversible actions execute), gate HOLD -> SUPERVISED (low-risk actions need approval), guest-guardrail or policy breach -> BOUNDED (recommend only).
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Maps the case study's authority ladder (p.14) to executable rules.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Simulation-day rates need at least 20 decisions before they can change the gate; below that they are reported with their sample size only.
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Rates from a handful of decisions are not evidence.

new_modeled_assumptions.assumption: Each context source read and each system write is one tool call.
new_modeled_assumptions.why: Needed to measure tool reliability per decision.
